questions.question: In which country is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.fun_fact: It stands in Paris and was built for a big fair in 1889.

questions.question: Which US president is the teddy bear named after?
questions.fun_fact: His nickname was Teddy. A toy shop made a bear toy after a famous story about him.

questions.question: In which mountains does Heidi live?
questions.fun_fact: Heidi lives with her grandfather high up on an Alp in Switzerland.

questions.question: How long does Earth take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.fun_fact: That trip is exactly why we have a year.

questions.question: Who has more bones, a baby or an adult?
questions.fun_fact: Babies have around 300 bones. Many grow together, so adults end up with 206.

questions.question: What are raisins?
questions.fun_fact: Take the water out of a grape and you get a raisin.

questions.question: How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
questions.fun_fact: Athletes train for years to take part.

questions.question: What force pulls things down to the ground?
questions.fun_fact: Without gravity you would float away from the floor.

questions.question: What is a group of flamingos called?
questions.fun_fact: Fitting for pink birds! A group of flamingos can also be called a stand.

questions.question: Which is the deepest place in the ocean?
questions.fun_fact: It is so deep that Mount Everest would fit inside with room to spare.

questions.question: Which color is NOT a color of the rainbow?
questions.fun_fact: A rainbow has red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fun_fact: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and one pumps it to the rest of the body. Octopus blood is blue.

questions.question: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fun_fact: Insects have six legs, so spiders are not insects at all.

questions.question: What does a thermometer measure?
questions.fun_fact: It tells you how hot or cold something is.

questions.question: Which vitamin can your skin make from sunshine?
questions.fun_fact: Vitamin D helps keep your bones strong.

questions.question: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
questions.fun_fact: It is a white palace-like tomb that took about 20 years to build.

questions.question: What is the usual order of keyboard letters called?
questions.fun_fact: The top row of letters starts with Q, W, E, R, T, Y.

questions.question: Which food can stay good for thousands of years?
questions.fun_fact: Honey found in old Egyptian tombs was still safe to eat.

questions.question: What does Rumpelstiltskin spin?
questions.fun_fact: He only gives up when somebody guesses his name.

questions.question: What is the Japanese art of paper folding called?
questions.fun_fact: With a single sheet of paper you can fold a crane or a frog.

questions.question: How many planets does our solar system have?
questions.fun_fact: Pluto used to count as the ninth, but is now called a dwarf planet.

questions.question: Where do potatoes grow?
questions.fun_fact: Potatoes are roots that swell under the soil. You dig them up.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.fun_fact: The Sun is a star. The next closest one is so far away that its light takes over four years to reach us.

questions.question: What happens to your pupils in the dark?
questions.fun_fact: Bigger pupils let in more light, so you can see a little better in the dark.

questions.question: Which sea animal has no brain?
questions.fun_fact: A jellyfish has a simple net of nerves instead of a brain.

questions.question: What does Cinderella lose at the ball?
questions.fun_fact: The prince searches the whole kingdom for the foot that fits the slipper.

questions.question: Which leaf is on the flag of Canada?
questions.fun_fact: Maple syrup also comes from Canada.

questions.question: What is the quiet middle of a hurricane called?
questions.fun_fact: It is calm in the eye, but the storm wall around it is very strong.

questions.question: In basketball, what do you throw the ball into?
questions.fun_fact: The hoop hangs 3.05 meters above the floor.

questions.question: Who is famous for making the light bulb useful?
questions.fun_fact: He and his team tried thousands of materials for the glowing thread.

questions.question: What color is the 'black box' on an airplane?
questions.fun_fact: The bright color makes it easy to find. It records data about the flight.

questions.question: Which is the biggest moon in our solar system?
questions.fun_fact: Ganymede circles Jupiter and is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.question: What is Peter Pan's fairy friend called?
questions.fun_fact: Tinker Bell is tiny and talks by ringing like a little bell.

questions.question: What makes soda fizzy?
questions.fun_fact: Carbon dioxide is pressed into the drink. It bubbles out when you open the bottle.

questions.question: How do you say 'goodbye' in Italian?
questions.fun_fact: Italians also say 'ciao' for both hello and goodbye.

questions.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.fun_fact: The five rings stand for the five parts of the world that take part.

questions.question: What is paper made from?
questions.fun_fact: Most paper is made from trees. Some is made from old paper.

questions.question: Which way does a compass needle point?
questions.fun_fact: The needle is a tiny magnet that follows Earth's magnetic field.

questions.question: Which is the longest bone in your body?
questions.fun_fact: The thigh bone is also one of the strongest bones you have.

questions.question: Which plant snaps shut to catch flies?
questions.fun_fact: It closes in a split second when an insect touches its tiny hairs.

questions.question: Which animal has the longest neck?
questions.fun_fact: A giraffe has the same number of neck bones as you: seven. Each one is just much longer.

questions.question: Which is the biggest continent?
questions.fun_fact: More than half of all people live in Asia.

questions.question: How many players of one soccer team are on the field?
questions.fun_fact: Each team also has a goalkeeper, who is one of the eleven.

questions.question: How many eyes does a honeybee have?
questions.fun_fact: A bee has two big eyes on the sides of its head and three small ones on top.

questions.question: What do plants need to make their food?
questions.fun_fact: Plants use light, water and air to make sugar. This is called photosynthesis.

questions.question: How many dwarfs live with Snow White?
questions.fun_fact: In the story of the Brothers Grimm they live in a little house in the woods.

questions.question: What is the front of a ship called?
questions.fun_fact: The back of the ship is called the stern.

questions.question: What does a magnifying glass do?
questions.fun_fact: Its curved glass bends the light so small things look large.

questions.question: Which of these is a fruit and not a vegetable?
questions.fun_fact: A fruit has seeds inside. Tomatoes do, so scientists call them fruit.

questions.question: Which planet spins on its side?
questions.fun_fact: Uranus rolls around the Sun almost like a ball.

questions.question: What color is a polar bear's skin under its fur?
questions.fun_fact: Black skin soaks up warmth from the sun. The fur only looks white.

questions.question: How many senses do people usually count?
questions.fun_fact: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

questions.question: Which of these fruits is a berry for scientists?
questions.fun_fact: Strawberries and raspberries are not true berries. Bananas are.

questions.question: Which animal sleeps hanging upside down?
questions.fun_fact: Bats hang by their feet, so they can just let go and fly off.

questions.question: What carries oxygen around in your blood?
questions.fun_fact: Red blood cells are what make your blood red.

questions.question: What do you add to dough to make bread rise?
questions.fun_fact: Yeast makes tiny gas bubbles that puff up the dough.

questions.question: Which writing uses raised dots that you feel with your fingers?
questions.fun_fact: Blind people read by touching the dots.

questions.question: What is the left side of a ship called?
questions.fun_fact: The right side is called starboard.

questions.question: Who wrote Peter Pan?
questions.fun_fact: He wrote it for the sons of a friend. He gave the story's rights to a children's hospital.

questions.question: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fun_fact: So the Sun you see in the sky is the Sun of 8 minutes ago.

questions.question: In which board game do you climb ladders and slide down snakes?
questions.fun_fact: The game comes from India, where it taught children about good and bad deeds.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain on Earth?
questions.fun_fact: Its top is almost nine kilometers above the sea.

questions.question: How do you say 'thank you' in French?
questions.fun_fact: The French say 'merci beaucoup' for 'thank you very much'.

questions.question: What is cheese made from?
questions.fun_fact: It takes about ten liters of milk to make one kilogram of cheese.

questions.question: In which city does the Wizard of Oz live?
questions.fun_fact: The whole city shines green, and visitors even wear green glasses.

questions.question: Butterflies can taste with their...?
questions.fun_fact: A butterfly lands on a leaf and tastes it with its feet to see if it is good for its eggs.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fun_fact: He stepped onto the Moon in 1969. Buzz Aldrin followed him a few minutes later.

questions.question: In which sport do you hit a puck?
questions.fun_fact: Players glide across the ice on skates.

questions.question: What makes leaves green?
questions.fun_fact: In autumn the green fades away, and the yellow and orange show through.

questions.question: An 11-year-old is said to have invented which cold treat?
questions.fun_fact: A boy left a drink with a stirring stick outside on a freezing night.

questions.question: What do ships drop to stay in one place?
questions.fun_fact: The heavy anchor digs into the sea floor.

questions.question: Which is the biggest organ of your body?
questions.fun_fact: Your skin covers your whole body and keeps germs out.

questions.question: Which planet is so light it could float in a giant bathtub?
questions.fun_fact: Saturn is mostly gas. On average it is lighter than water.

questions.question: What did Johannes Gutenberg invent in the 1400s?
questions.fun_fact: Thanks to his press, books got cheaper and more people learned to read.

questions.question: Which is the biggest ocean on Earth?
questions.fun_fact: The Pacific Ocean is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.

questions.question: Which animal is the fastest on land?
questions.fun_fact: A cheetah can reach about 100 km/h in a short sprint, but it gets tired fast.

questions.question: How many moons does Mars have?
questions.fun_fact: They are called Phobos and Deimos, and they are small and shaped like potatoes.

questions.question: Which organ do you think with?
questions.fun_fact: Your brain uses about a fifth of all the energy your body makes.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fun_fact: Many people guess Sydney, but Canberra was built just to be the capital.

questions.question: How many players of one team are on the court in basketball?
questions.fun_fact: Teams also have players waiting on the bench.

questions.question: What do the wheels of a train roll on?
questions.fun_fact: Two steel rails guide the train, so it does not need to be steered.

questions.question: What does the pasta name 'vermicelli' mean in Italian?
questions.fun_fact: The long thin strings of pasta reminded people of little worms.

questions.question: Who blows the houses down in The Three Little Pigs?
questions.fun_fact: The third little pig builds a house of bricks, and that one stays standing.

questions.question: What is a baby frog called?
questions.fun_fact: A tadpole breathes with gills and has a tail. Later it grows legs.

questions.question: How many rooms (chambers) does a human heart have?
questions.fun_fact: Two small rooms on top and two big ones below.

questions.question: Who is the boy raised by wolves in The Jungle Book?
questions.fun_fact: His friends in the jungle are Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther.

questions.question: Which two brothers built the first successful airplane?
questions.fun_fact: Their first flight in 1903 lasted only twelve seconds.

questions.question: How many continents are there?
questions.fun_fact: They are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America.

questions.question: Which vegetable can make you cry when you cut it?
questions.fun_fact: Onions release a gas that stings your eyes. A cold onion stings less.

questions.question: How many sides does a normal die have?
questions.fun_fact: Dice with other numbers of sides are used in some board games.

questions.question: Which bird lays the biggest egg?
questions.fun_fact: One ostrich egg weighs as much as about 20 chicken eggs.

questions.question: In which country was paper invented?
questions.fun_fact: People in China made paper about 2,000 years ago.

questions.question: Which planet has a day that is longer than its year?
questions.fun_fact: Venus turns so slowly that one spin takes longer than one trip around the Sun.

questions.question: Which language do people in Brazil speak?
questions.fun_fact: Brazil is the biggest country in South America.

questions.question: Which bird cannot fly but is a great swimmer?
questions.fun_fact: Penguins use their wings like flippers to zoom through the water.

questions.question: What is the tallest type of tree in the world?
questions.fun_fact: Some redwoods grow taller than 100 meters.

questions.question: How far is a marathon, about?
questions.fun_fact: The distance is exactly 42.195 km. In miles, it is about 26.

questions.question: What is chocolate made from?
questions.fun_fact: Cocoa beans grow inside big pods on cocoa trees.

questions.question: Where is the smallest bone in your body?
questions.fun_fact: The stirrup bone is about as big as a grain of rice.

questions.question: Which flying machine has blades that spin on top?
questions.fun_fact: The spinning blades lift it straight up. It can hover in one place.

questions.question: What causes the tides in the oceans?
questions.fun_fact: The Moon tugs on the water, so the sea rises and falls twice a day.

questions.question: Which animal wins the race against the hare?
questions.fun_fact: The hare naps in the middle of the race. Slow and steady wins.

questions.question: Which tool do you use to see far-away stars better?
questions.fun_fact: Galileo used one to discover moons around Jupiter.

questions.question: Which of these animals has rectangular pupils?
questions.fun_fact: Sideways pupils give goats a wide view, so they can spot danger from far away.

questions.question: Who wrote The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling?
questions.fun_fact: He was born in Denmark and wrote more than 150 fairy tales.

questions.question: Which planet is the biggest?
questions.fun_fact: More than 1,000 Earths would fit inside Jupiter.

questions.question: What do you call a person who does not eat meat?
questions.fun_fact: Vegetarians still eat things like vegetables, fruit and cheese.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
questions.fun_fact: Your heart is about as big as your fist and beats all day and night.

questions.question: Who flies an airplane?
questions.fun_fact: Big airplanes usually have two pilots in the cockpit.

questions.question: How many keys does a standard piano have?
questions.fun_fact: 52 of the keys are white and 36 are black.

questions.question: What do the numbers on opposite sides of a die add up to?
questions.fun_fact: One is opposite six, two is opposite five, and three is opposite four.

questions.question: What does the short hand on a clock show?
questions.fun_fact: The long hand shows the minutes.

questions.question: Which is the biggest desert in the world?
questions.fun_fact: A desert is a place with very little rain. Antarctica is a cold desert.

questions.question: Which country looks like a boot on the map?
questions.fun_fact: It even seems to kick the island of Sicily.

questions.question: Pizza comes from which country?
questions.fun_fact: The first pizzas were baked in the Italian city of Naples.

questions.question: How many milk teeth do children usually have?
questions.fun_fact: Adults have 32 teeth. Milk teeth fall out to make room for the bigger ones.

questions.question: Why does a hot air balloon rise?
questions.fun_fact: The air inside is warmed by a burner, so it is lighter than the cool air outside.

questions.question: Which country has a flag that is not a rectangle?
questions.fun_fact: Its flag is made of two stacked triangles.

questions.question: Which plant can grow almost a meter in one day?
questions.fun_fact: Some bamboo grows so fast that you could almost watch it get taller.

questions.question: What is the name of our galaxy?
questions.fun_fact: It holds hundreds of billions of stars, and our Sun is just one of them.

questions.question: Which chess piece moves in an L shape?
questions.fun_fact: It is the only piece that can jump over others.

questions.question: Which invention lets you talk to a friend far away?
questions.fun_fact: Alexander Graham Bell made the first working one in 1876.

questions.question: Which animal sleeps up to 20 hours a day?
questions.fun_fact: Eucalyptus leaves give little energy, so koalas rest a lot. Giraffes sleep only a few hours.

questions.question: What did Jack get for his cow?
questions.fun_fact: The beans grew into a giant beanstalk overnight.

questions.question: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.fun_fact: Mars is covered in dust that contains rusty iron.

questions.question: What is guacamole mainly made from?
questions.fun_fact: Guacamole comes from Mexico. It is great with tortilla chips.

questions.question: How many arms does a typical snowflake have?
questions.fun_fact: Snowflakes all have six sides, but no two look exactly the same.

questions.question: Which country has the Pyramids of Giza?
questions.fun_fact: The biggest one is more than 4,500 years old.

questions.question: In which country were the first Olympic Games held?
questions.fun_fact: They started more than 2,700 years ago in a place called Olympia.

questions.question: What is the hardest part of your body?
questions.fun_fact: Enamel is even harder than bone. That is why you must brush your teeth.

questions.question: Where does a baby kangaroo grow up in its first months?
questions.fun_fact: A newborn joey is tiny, about as big as a jelly bean. It crawls into the pouch by itself.

questions.question: What was the very first computer mouse made of?
questions.fun_fact: Douglas Engelbart built it in the 1960s. It had two wheels and a wooden shell.

questions.question: Who wrote Pippi Longstocking?
questions.fun_fact: Pippi is the strongest girl in the world and lives with a horse and a monkey.

questions.question: What does a speedometer show?
questions.fun_fact: Most cars show it with a needle or a number.

questions.question: How do you say 'hello' in Spanish?
questions.fun_fact: Spanish is spoken in Spain and in most of Latin America.

questions.question: Why can't you hear sounds in space?
questions.fun_fact: Sound needs air to travel through, and space is almost empty.

questions.question: What does a periscope help you do?
questions.fun_fact: Submarines use it to look around while they stay under water.

questions.question: Which of these animals can sleep standing up?
questions.fun_fact: Horses can lock their leg joints, so they can doze without falling over.

questions.question: What makes popcorn pop?
questions.fun_fact: The tiny drop of water inside turns to steam until the kernel bursts.

questions.question: Which tree do acorns grow on?
questions.fun_fact: Squirrels bury acorns and forget some, so new oak trees sprout.

questions.question: What color is your blood inside your veins?
questions.fun_fact: Veins only look blue through your skin. The blood in them is dark red.

questions.question: Which boy can fly and never grows up?
questions.fun_fact: He lives in Neverland with the Lost Boys.

questions.question: How many squares are on a chessboard?
questions.fun_fact: The board has eight rows of eight squares. Each player starts with 16 pieces on it.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.fun_fact: Cows, rabbits and elephants are all herbivores.

questions.question: In Hansel and Gretel, what is the witch's house made of?
questions.fun_fact: The children nibble on the walls without asking.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest?
questions.fun_fact: Venus is wrapped in thick air that traps heat, so it is hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: What does a magnet stick to?
questions.fun_fact: Steel is made from iron, so magnets stick to it.

questions.question: What is a baby dog called?
questions.fun_fact: Puppies are born with their eyes closed and open them after about two weeks.

questions.question: Which desert is the biggest hot desert?
questions.fun_fact: The Sahara is about as big as the whole United States.

questions.question: Which is the only mammal that can really fly?
questions.fun_fact: Flying squirrels and gliders only glide. Bats flap their wings like birds.

questions.question: What does Pinocchio's nose do when he lies?
questions.fun_fact: Pinocchio is a wooden puppet who wants to become a real boy.

questions.question: Which is the smallest country in the world?
questions.fun_fact: You could walk across it in a few minutes.

questions.question: What does the Moon travel around?
questions.fun_fact: The Moon needs about a month for one trip around Earth.

questions.question: In what unit do ships measure their speed?
questions.fun_fact: One knot is about 1.85 kilometers per hour.

questions.question: Whom does Alice follow down the rabbit hole?
questions.fun_fact: The rabbit is always worried that he is late.

questions.question: What is a shooting star really?
questions.fun_fact: It burns up when it zooms into our air. Most are no bigger than a pebble.

questions.question: What is a baby cow called?
questions.fun_fact: A baby horse is a foal and a baby sheep is a lamb.

questions.question: Which animal has fingerprints almost like ours?
questions.fun_fact: Koala fingerprints look so much like human ones that they are hard to tell apart.

questions.question: What does the Ugly Duckling grow up to be?
questions.fun_fact: He was never ugly. He was just a swan among ducks.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its big rings?
questions.fun_fact: The rings are made of countless chunks of ice and rock.
